'''Ernst Christian Julius Schering''' (13 July 1833 – 2 November 1897) was a German [[mathematician]].

==Early life and career==
Born in 1833 near [[Bleckede]] at the [[Elbe]] as the son of a forester, he attended [[Realschule]] ("Johanneum") in [[Lüneburg]] from 1845 to 1850, where he already showed a certain talent for mathematics. With the intention to engage in architectural engineering, he attended the [[University of Hanover|Hannover Polytechnic]] from 1850 to 1852. 

==At the University of Göttingen==
Following a fondness of mathematics and physics, in 1852, at the age of 19, he moved on to study in [[Göttingen]], attending classes by [[Carl Friedrich Gauss|Gauß]], [[Wilhelm Eduard Weber|Weber]], [[Peter Gustav Lejeune Dirichlet|Dirichlet]], [[Moritz Abraham Stern|Stern]] and [[Bernhard Riemann|Riemann]]. In 1857, he received a [[doctoral degree]] for his award-winning manuscript "Zur mathematischen Theorie electrischer Ströme" ("On the mathematical theory of electric currents"). In 1858, he [[Habilitation|habilitated]] based on his work "Über die conforme Abbildung des Ellipsoids auf der Ebene" ("On the conformal mapping of the ellipsoid on the plane").

After turning down a call to [[Gießen]] in 1860, he was appointed associate professor, and he became a member of the [[Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities|Königliche Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen (Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities)]] in 1862. From 1860 onwards he was also appointed by the Göttingen Academy to edit the works of [[Carl Friedrich Gauss|Gauß]], of which he eventually completed six volumes.

During the 1860s he was appointed by the hanoverian government as a member of a commission for the European [[arc measurement]]. In 1868, management of the [[Göttingen Observatory]] was divided into two divisions, one for practical astronomy and one for theoretical astronomy, [[geodesy]] and mathematical physics, of which Schering took over the former division from [[Wilhelm Klinkerfues]] and was appointed full professor. Among other observations, he was particularly busy with magnetic observations in connection with the [[:de:Erstes Internationales Polarjahr|polar expeditions in 1882/1883]].

==Family==
His younger brother [[:de:Karl Schering|Karl Schering]]
also studied physics and mathematics in Göttingen. He later became professor of mathematics at the [[University of Strasbourg]]
and subsequently professor of physics at the [[Technical University of Darmstadt]]. His wife, Maria Heliodora, whom he married in 1876, was the daughter of the Swedish mathematician [[Carl Johan Malmsten]]. They had one daughter and two sons, one of which, physicist [[Harald Schering]], would later become professor of electrical engineering at the [[Technische Hochschule Hannover]].
